**Vaidya spacetime — the simplest dynamical black hole**

The **Vaidya metric** (named after Indian physicist Prahalad Chunnilal Vaidya) is an exact solution to Einstein’s equations that describes a **black hole forming from collapsing radiation**.

It is the gravitational version of a “light bulb turning on” in spacetime: before a certain moment everything is flat; after that moment a black hole exists.

### Physical picture (the null shell)

Imagine a thin spherical shell of **null dust** (massless radiation or light-like matter) falling inward at the speed of light.

- For advanced time v\<0 v \< 0 v\<0, the shell has not yet arrived → spacetime is completely flat (Minkowski). 

- At v=0 v = 0 v=0, the entire shell reaches the origin and instantly creates a mass M M M. 

- For v\>0 v \> 0 v\>0, you have a Schwarzschild black hole of mass M M M. 

Because the shell moves at the speed of light, it is called a **null shell**. Nothing can outrun it. As soon as the shell passes a given radius, that region “knows” the mass is there and an event horizon forms right behind the shell.

This is the simplest possible model of **black hole formation** that is still an exact solution of general relativity.

### The metric in words

In coordinates adapted to the incoming radiation (advanced Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates), the line element is:

ds2=−(1−2GM(v)r)dv2+2 dv dr+r2dΩ2ds^2 = -\\left(1 - \\frac\{2GM(v)\}\{r\}\\right) dv^2 + 2\\, dv\\, dr + r^2 d\\Omega^2ds2=−(1−r2GM(v)​)dv2+2dvdr+r2dΩ2

Here is what every symbol means:

- v v v = advanced time (think of it as the time a light ray traveling inward would measure). 

- r r r = radial coordinate (distance from the center). 

- M(v) M(v) M(v) = the mass function. In the classic collapsing-shell case it is a step function: M(v)=0 M(v) = 0 M(v)=0 for v\<0 v \< 0 v\<0 and M(v)=M M(v) = M M(v)=M (constant) for v\>0 v \> 0 v\>0. 

- dΩ2 d\\Omega^2 dΩ2 = the usual angular part on the sphere (dθ2+sin⁡2θ dϕ2 d\\theta^2 + \\sin^2\\theta\\, d\\phi^2 dθ2+sin2θdϕ2). 

The key feature is that the mass appears only through the function M(v)  M(v)  M(v). When M(v)  M(v)  M(v) jumps from 0 to M  M  M at v=0  v = 0  v=0, a horizon instantly forms at r=2GM  r = 2GM  r=2GM.

### What the horizon does

- Before the shell arrives (v\<0 v \< 0 v\<0): no horizon, light can escape from any radius. 

- After the shell passes a given point: an event horizon appears at r=2GM r = 2GM r=2GM. Light rays exactly at that radius stay there forever; anything inside is trapped. 

Because the shell is null, the horizon forms **immediately** behind the shell — there is no delay. This makes the Vaidya solution the cleanest toy model for studying how a horizon appears and how quantum fields behave on it (including Hawking radiation).

### Why physicists (and the paper) love Vaidya

- It is **exact** — no approximations. 

- It is **dynamical** — the spacetime is changing with time (unlike static Schwarzschild). 

- It has a **clear formation history** — you can unambiguously say “before this moment there was no black hole.” 

- It is simple enough that many calculations (ray tracing, quantum field theory on curved space, etc.) can be done analytically. 

In the paper you asked about, the authors take exactly this Vaidya collapsing shell and construct its **electromagnetic single copy** — a collapsing shell of charge in flat space whose “double copy” is the gravitational Vaidya solution. That lets them compute particle production in ordinary flat-space electromagnetism and then translate the result into the corresponding Hawking radiation in the gravitational Vaidya spacetime.

### Everyday analogy that fits the engineering mindset

Think of a fiber-optic network that suddenly receives a massive burst of traffic exactly at one moment (a “null shell” of data packets all arriving together).

- Before the burst: the network is quiet and everything can flow freely. 

- At the instant the burst hits the central router: a permanent “congestion zone” (the horizon) forms. Any new packets that enter that zone can never get out again. 

- After the burst: the router behaves like a black hole for all further traffic that falls inside the congestion radius. 

Vaidya is the gravitational version of that sudden, permanent traffic jam forming from an incoming light-speed wall of data.

Here is a careful, step-by-step unpacking of what the authors actually do in the core technical part of the paper. I will introduce only new background concepts we have not already covered and translate the calculations into ordinary language.

### Overall goal of this section in the paper

The authors want to show that you can compute something that looks like Hawking radiation **entirely in flat space** using ordinary quantum field theory, then use the double-copy dictionary to read off the gravitational result.

They do this by scattering a simple probe particle off the electromagnetic single-copy background of Vaidya. They calculate the scattering in two completely different ways (full Feynman diagrams + resummation, and semiclassical ray tracing) and show that both methods give exactly the same answer. That answer turns out to have a thermal spectrum whose temperature is the double-copy image of the Hawking temperature.

### New background concepts needed here

**Massless charged scalar field**  
A “scalar” is the simplest possible field — it has no spin and no polarization. It is just a number at every point in space (like a temperature field or a sound-wave amplitude). Making it “charged” means it feels the electromagnetic force, so it couples to the vector potential Aμ  A\_\\mu  Aμ​. “Massless” means it travels at the speed of light.

They choose this probe because it is the simplest thing that still feels the background electromagnetic field and can be created or destroyed by it. Using a scalar avoids all the extra complications of spin that electrons or photons would bring.

**Wave packet with impact parameter**  
Instead of sending in a single plane wave, they send in a localized “blob” of the scalar field that travels along a straight line before it feels the background. The line misses the origin by a distance called the **impact parameter** b  b  b. Because the background turns on at a definite advanced time v=0  v = 0  v=0, the wave packet is chosen so that it arrives from the past with support only before the shell passes.

**Geometric-optics (eikonal) limit**  
They work in the high-frequency, small-deflection regime. The wavelength of the probe is much shorter than any other length scale in the problem (the impact parameter, the size of the charge distribution, etc.). In this limit, the wave behaves almost like a classical ray, and quantum interference effects are controlled. This is the same regime in which light rays follow Snell’s law in a slowly varying medium.

**Kerr-Schild form and why A2=0  A^2 = 0  A2=0 matters**  
The electromagnetic single-copy background is written in a special gauge (Kerr-Schild) where the vector potential satisfies AμAμ=0  A\_\\mu A^\\mu = 0  Aμ​Aμ=0. This is not true for a general electromagnetic field. Because of this property, when the charged scalar interacts with the background, there are **no four-point “seagull” contact vertices**. The only interactions are cubic (scalar emits or absorbs one photon from the background at a time). This makes the Feynman diagrams much simpler — they form clean ladders with no extra rungs connecting in complicated ways.

### What the authors actually calculate (step by step in English)

**Step 1: Set up the background**  
They take the single-copy electromagnetic field that corresponds to the collapsing Vaidya shell. Before advanced time v=0  v = 0  v=0 the field is zero. After v=0  v = 0  v=0 a Coulomb field suddenly appears, centered at the origin, as if a spherical shell of charge has collapsed to a point. The probe scalar wave packet is sent in from past null infinity along a straight line that passes the origin at a finite impact parameter, and the wave packet is timed so that it only exists before the shell arrives.

**Step 2: Tree-level scattering (single photon exchange)**  
At lowest order the scalar can exchange one photon with the background charge distribution. Because the background is static after v=0  v = 0  v=0 and falls off as 1/r  1/r  1/r, the phase the wave picks up while traveling past the charge is obtained by integrating the vector potential along the straight-line path.

That integral produces a **logarithmic phase** that depends on how early or late the wave packet arrives relative to the shell (the variable v  v  v). The phase looks like log⁡(−v/μ)  \\log(-v / \\mu)  log(−v/μ), where μ  \\mu  μ is an arbitrary scale that drops out of physical quantities. This is the same kind of phase you get in ordinary Coulomb scattering, but here the “Coulomb center” only exists after v=0  v = 0  v=0.

**Step 3: Higher-order ladder diagrams**  
The scalar can exchange any number of photons with the background. Because the background is in Kerr-Schild form, these exchanges form simple **ladder diagrams** (the scalar line goes straight, and photons are exchanged one after another with the background). There are no crossed diagrams or contact terms that would complicate the counting.

In the geometric-optics limit these ladders can be resummed exactly. Each additional rung contributes a factor that is proportional to the same logarithmic phase. Because the rungs commute with each other in this kinematics, the sum over any number of rungs collapses into an exponential:

The total phase factor becomes exp⁡(2iαlog⁡(−v/μ))  \\exp(2i \\alpha \\log(-v / \\mu))  exp(2iαlog(−v/μ)), where the single number α=QQB/(4π)  \\alpha = Q Q\_B / (4\\pi)  α=QQB​/(4π) encodes the product of the probe charge Q  Q  Q and the background charge strength QB  Q\_B  QB​.

This is an all-orders result in the coupling to the background. It is non-perturbative in that sense, even though each individual diagram is perturbative.

From this expression they read off two coefficients:

- The coefficient that multiplies the positive-frequency outgoing wave → this is the Bogoliubov α \\alpha α 

- The coefficient that multiplies the negative-frequency outgoing wave → this is the Bogoliubov β \\beta β 

These α  \\alpha  α and β  \\beta  β tell you how much the incoming positive-frequency mode mixes with outgoing negative-frequency modes. That mixing is exactly what produces real particles from the vacuum when the background is time-dependent.

**Step 5: Semiclassical ray-tracing calculation (completely independent check)**  
Instead of using Feynman diagrams at all, they solve the classical problem of a charged massless particle (or high-frequency wave) traveling through the same time-dependent electromagnetic background. They compute the total phase the particle accumulates by integrating the action along the actual trajectory (which feels the Lorentz force from the background).

They have two completely independent calculations (infinite series of Feynman diagrams resummed, and classical ray tracing) that agree exactly in the geometric-optics limit. Both give a thermal particle spectrum whose temperature is controlled by the charge strength of the background. Because the background is the single copy of Vaidya, that temperature is the double-copy image of the Hawking temperature of the gravitational black hole.

This is the concrete technical heart of the paper: they have exhibited a flat-space electromagnetic calculation whose result, when translated by the double-copy dictionary, becomes Hawking radiation.

**Hawking Temperature — explained clearly**

Hawking radiation is the surprising fact that black holes are not completely black. They slowly emit thermal radiation and therefore have a temperature. That temperature is called the **Hawking temperature**.

### The simple formula

For a non-rotating, uncharged black hole of mass M  M  M (Schwarzschild black hole), the Hawking temperature is

TH=18πGMT\_H = \\frac\{1\}\{8\\pi G M\}TH​=8πGM1​

(in units where ℏ=c=kB=1  \\hbar = c = k\_B = 1  ℏ=c=kB​=1).

Here:

- G G G is Newton’s gravitational constant. 

- M M M is the mass of the black hole. 

- The factor 8π 8\\pi 8π comes from the precise calculation involving the surface gravity of the horizon. 

The key point is that **smaller black holes are hotter**. A black hole with half the mass has twice the temperature. This is the opposite of everyday intuition (bigger objects are usually colder), but it is a direct consequence of quantum mechanics near the horizon.

### What “temperature” actually means for a black hole

Temperature tells you the average energy of the particles that are being emitted.

When a black hole radiates, it does **not** emit particles with a random spread of energies. The particles come out with a precise **thermal (blackbody) spectrum** — exactly the same distribution you would measure coming from a hot oven or a star. The number of particles at energy E  E  E follows

n(E)=1eE/TH−1n(E) = \\frac\{1\}\{e^\{E / T\_H\} - 1\}n(E)=eE/TH​−11​

(for bosons). This is the same shape we discussed earlier in the electromagnetic single-copy calculation. The only difference is that on the gravitational side the temperature is fixed by the mass M  M  M through the formula above.

### Why does a black hole have a temperature at all?

The basic picture (without heavy math) is this:

Near the event horizon, quantum fields are constantly producing **virtual particle–antiparticle pairs** (this is normal vacuum fluctuations). Normally these pairs annihilate almost immediately and disappear.

However, right at the horizon something special happens:

- One member of the pair can fall into the black hole. 

- The other member can escape to infinity as a real particle. 

From the outside observer’s point of view, it looks as if the black hole is emitting particles. Because the process is controlled by the geometry of the horizon, the escaping particles have a thermal distribution whose temperature is set by how “strong” the horizon’s gravitational pull is (the surface gravity).

In the Vaidya case we have been discussing, the horizon forms suddenly when the null shell collapses. The same pair-creation process occurs, and the temperature that appears is exactly the Hawking temperature corresponding to the mass that was created.

### Surface gravity — the real origin of the temperature

The temperature is not put in by hand. It comes from a quantity called **surface gravity** κ  \\kappa  κ:

TH=κ2πT\_H = \\frac\{\\kappa\}\{2\\pi\}TH​=2πκ​

Surface gravity κ  \\kappa  κ is the acceleration that an observer hovering just outside the horizon would feel (redshifted to infinity). For a Schwarzschild black hole it is simply

κ=14GM.\\kappa = \\frac\{1\}\{4 G M\}.κ=4GM1​.

So the temperature is directly proportional to how strong the gravitational field is right at the horizon. Stronger gravity (smaller black hole) → higher temperature.

### Connection to the paper and the double-copy calculation

In the electromagnetic single-copy problem, the authors found a thermal spectrum whose temperature was set by the parameter α∝QB  \\alpha \\propto Q\_B  α∝QB​ (how strong the collapsing charge shell is).

When they apply the double-copy map:

- The charge strength QB Q\_B QB​ is replaced by the mass M M M of the black hole. 

- The electromagnetic temperature parameter is therefore replaced by the surface gravity κ=1/(4GM) \\kappa = 1/(4 G M) κ=1/(4GM). 

- The temperature they computed in flat-space electromagnetism is therefore **exactly** the Hawking temperature TH=κ/(2π) T\_H = \\kappa / (2\\pi) TH​=κ/(2π) of the gravitational black hole that forms. 

This is why they can say the temperature found in the electromagnetic calculation is “the double-copy image” of the real Hawking temperature. The calculation never used curved spacetime or general relativity directly — the double-copy dictionary translated the flat-space result into the correct gravitational answer.

### Why this is important

- It shows that black holes are thermodynamic objects. They have temperature, entropy (Bekenstein-Hawking entropy), and they can evaporate. 

- For tiny black holes (near the Planck mass), TH T\_H TH​ becomes enormous and evaporation is extremely rapid. 

- The fact that the same thermal spectrum emerges from a much simpler electromagnetic calculation (via double copy) suggests that thermality has a deeper algebraic origin that is visible already in gauge theory. 

In short: the Hawking temperature is the temperature of the radiation that a black hole must emit because of quantum effects right at its horizon. Its value is fixed by the surface gravity, which for an ordinary black hole is inversely proportional to its mass. In the paper we have been analyzing, this temperature appears automatically in the flat-space electromagnetic proxy calculation, and the double copy tells you it is the correct Hawking temperature of the resulting gravitational black hole.

**Kinematic factors — what they actually contain**

We already know that in gauge-theory Feynman diagrams the full contribution splits into:

**Diagram = (color factor) × (kinematic factor) / (propagators)**

The **kinematic factor** (often called *N*) is the part that lives entirely in **spacetime**. It carries all the information about how the particles are moving and how their “directions” or “orientations” interact.

Here’s what actually lives inside a kinematic factor, in plain language:

### 1. Momenta of the particles

Every external particle brings its own 4-momentum (energy + 3-momentum vector). These appear as dot products like:

- p1⋅p2 p\_1 \\cdot p\_2 p1​⋅p2​ (how much the momenta of two particles are aligned) 

- pμ p^\\mu pμ contracted with other objects 

These dot products tell you the **energy flow** and **angle** between particles. In the high-energy (eikonal) limit we used in the paper, many of these simplify dramatically.

### 2. Polarization vectors / tensors

This is the “orientation” information:

- For photons or gluons (spin-1): a polarization vector εμ \\varepsilon^\\mu εμ. It describes whether the wave is oscillating horizontally, vertically, or in some other direction. 

- For gravitons (spin-2): a polarization **tensor** εμν \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\} εμν. It has two indices because the graviton has two “directions” of stretching/squeezing. 

The kinematic factor contains many terms like:

- ε1⋅ε2 \\varepsilon\_1 \\cdot \\varepsilon\_2 ε1​⋅ε2​ (how two polarization vectors align with each other) 

- ε⋅p \\varepsilon \\cdot p ε⋅p (how a polarization vector points relative to a momentum) 

These are exactly the pieces that become much more complicated when you go from gluons to gravitons.

### 3. Lorentz index contractions (using the metric)

All the vectors and tensors above have Lorentz indices (μ,ν=0,1,2,3  \\mu, \\nu = 0,1,2,3  μ,ν=0,1,2,3). The kinematic factor contains the rules for how these indices are connected using the metric tensor ημν  \\eta\_\{\\mu\\nu\}  ημν​.

Think of it as the “wiring diagram” that tells you which index from one vertex connects to which index on the next propagator or vertex. Every free index eventually gets summed over (contracted) so the final answer is a pure number.

### 4. Vertex structures from the Feynman rules

Each interaction point (vertex) contributes its own specific tensor structure made of momenta and polarizations.

**Simple example (3-gluon vertex in Yang-Mills):**  
The kinematic part of the 3-gluon vertex contains terms like:

ε1⋅ε2 (p1−p2)⋅ε3+cyclic permutations\\varepsilon\_1 \\cdot \\varepsilon\_2 \\, (p\_1 - p\_2) \\cdot \\varepsilon\_3 + \\text\{cyclic permutations\}ε1​⋅ε2​(p1​−p2​)⋅ε3​+cyclic permutations

This expression encodes momentum conservation and how the three polarization vectors “talk” to each other at the interaction point. It is built only from dot products and is completely independent of color.

When you do the double copy, you take this entire kinematic expression and treat it as if it were a second “color factor.” That’s how you build the much more complicated 3-graviton vertex.

### 5. What it looks like in the eikonal / geometric-optics limit (the regime used in the paper)

In the high-frequency, small-deflection limit we discussed for the Vaidya single-copy calculation, the kinematic factor simplifies enormously.

Instead of a huge tensor expression, it often reduces to a **phase** that the wave accumulates while traveling past the background:

- The phase is obtained by integrating the background field along a nearly straight trajectory. 

- In the paper this gave the logarithmic phase log⁡(−v/μ) \\log(-v / \\mu) log(−v/μ). 

- All the complicated index and polarization structure collapses into this single complex number that depends on the arrival time v v v. 

This is why the resummation became possible — the kinematic factors from each ladder rung were essentially the same and could be added coherently.

### Engineering-style analogy

Imagine you are sending signals through a multi-core processor’s interconnect:

- The **color factor** is like the routing tag or core-ID that decides *which cores are allowed to talk*. 

- The **kinematic factor** is the actual electrical waveform: its voltage levels, timing edges, differential signaling, clock skew, and how the signal distorts as it travels down the wire. 

When you “double copy,” you are effectively saying: “Take the electrical waveform rules and use them in place of the routing tags.” The resulting system obeys a new, more complex set of consistency rules — exactly what happens when you go from Yang-Mills to gravity.

### Why this matters for the double copy

The reason the double copy works is that the kinematic factor *N* obeys the **same algebraic identities** (Jacobi identity, antisymmetry) as the color factor. Because of that, you can replace the color label with a second copy of *N* and the whole object remains consistent. That replacement turns gluon scattering into graviton scattering and turns the electromagnetic single-copy background into the gravitational Vaidya solution.

**Polarization in Gravitons — explained from the LIGO picture onward**

You already know from LIGO that gravitational waves have **two polarization modes** called **plus (+)** and **cross (×)**. These are the only two independent ways a gravitational wave can stretch and squeeze spacetime as it passes. Let’s build on that and go deeper.

### 1. What polarization actually means for gravitational waves

When a gravitational wave travels through space, it doesn’t carry energy by pushing particles like sound or electromagnetic waves do in a simple way. Instead, it **changes the geometry of spacetime itself**.

As the wave passes:

- Distances between objects are periodically stretched in one direction and squeezed in the perpendicular direction. 

- Then the pattern rotates or switches. 

LIGO detects this by measuring tiny changes in the length of its two perpendicular arms. The **plus polarization** stretches one arm while squeezing the other. The **cross polarization** does the same thing but rotated by 45 degrees.

These two patterns are independent — you can have a wave that is purely plus, purely cross, or any combination of the two.

### 2. Why gravitons have polarization (spin-2)

Photons (spin-1) have **two** polarization states (horizontal and vertical, or left- and right-circular).  
Gravitons are **spin-2** particles. In four-dimensional spacetime, a massless spin-2 particle has **exactly two** physical polarization states.

This is not arbitrary. It comes from the fact that the graviton is described by a **symmetric tensor field** hμν  h^\{\\mu\\nu\}  hμν (the small perturbation of the metric). A general symmetric tensor in 4D has 10 components, but most of them are not physical:

- Some are removed by **gauge freedom** (coordinate choices — similar to how we can choose the Coulomb gauge in electromagnetism). 

- Some are removed because the wave must be **transverse** (no component along the direction of travel). 

- Some are removed because it must be **traceless** (the overall stretching and squeezing must balance out — volume is preserved to first order). 

After all these conditions, exactly **two** independent degrees of freedom remain. These are the plus and cross modes you see in LIGO.

### 3. The polarization tensor εμν \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\} εμν

In theoretical calculations (Feynman diagrams, scattering amplitudes, etc.), each external graviton is described by a **polarization tensor** εμν(p)  \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\}(p)  εμν(p), where:

- p p p is the 4-momentum of the graviton (its direction of travel and energy). 

- εμν \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\} εμν is a symmetric, traceless, transverse tensor that encodes which polarization mode the graviton is in. 

For a wave traveling in the z-direction:

- The **plus** mode has non-zero components only in the x-y plane in a specific pattern (stretching x while squeezing y). 

- The **cross** mode has non-zero components rotated by 45° (stretching along the diagonals). 

These two tensors are the only independent solutions that satisfy all the physical requirements.

### 4. How polarization enters the kinematic factor

Going back to our earlier discussion on **kinematic factors**:

The kinematic numerator N  N  N for a graviton process contains many contractions involving the polarization tensors, such as:

- ε1μνε2μν \\varepsilon\_1^\{\\mu\\nu\} \\varepsilon\_\{2\\mu\\nu\} ε1μν​ε2μν​ (how much two gravitons’ polarizations overlap) 

- εμνpμpν \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\} p\_\\mu p\_\\nu εμνpμ​pν​ terms (how the polarization aligns with the momentum) 

- More complicated index structures coming from the 3-graviton or 4-graviton vertices 

When you do the **double copy**, these polarization structures get built automatically from the simpler polarization vectors of gluons. That’s one reason the double-copy procedure is so powerful — it generates the correct graviton polarization behavior without having to derive the complicated gravity vertices from scratch.

### 5. Why only two modes matter physically

Even though the mathematical object hμν  h^\{\\mu\\nu\}  hμν has many components, only the two physical modes (+ and ×) carry energy and can be detected at large distances. The other components are either:

- Pure gauge (they can be removed by changing coordinates), or 

- Non-propagating (they fall off too quickly or don’t travel at the speed of light). 

This is analogous to how, in electromagnetism, we can choose a gauge where only the two transverse photon polarizations remain physical.

### 6. Connection to LIGO and real observations

LIGO’s two arms are oriented at 90° to each other precisely to be sensitive to these two modes. A plus-polarized wave will lengthen one arm while shortening the other. A cross-polarized wave does the same but at 45° to the arms. By combining signals from multiple detectors (LIGO Hanford + Livingston + Virgo), scientists can reconstruct both the strength and the polarization content of the wave, which gives information about the orientation of the merging black holes or neutron stars.

### Quick summary

| **Property** | **Photon (spin-1)** | Graviton (spin-2) |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Number of physical polarizations | 2 | 2 |
| Polarization object | Vector εμ \\varepsilon^\\mu εμ | Tensor εμν \\varepsilon^\{\\mu\\nu\} εμν |
| Physical effect | Oscillating E and B fields | Stretching/squeezing of distances |
| Independent modes | Horizontal / Vertical | Plus (+) / Cross (×) |
| Detected by | Antennas, eyes, etc. | LIGO, Virgo, future detectors |

where a+  a\_+  a+​ and a×  a\_\\times  a×​ are just numbers that tell you how much of each mode is present. This is exactly analogous to how any light wave can be written as a combination of horizontal and vertical polarization.

If both are purely plus mode and aligned, this overlap is maximum. If one is plus and the other is cross, the overlap is zero.

This is why LIGO can distinguish the two modes — they produce different patterns of stretching, and the theoretical calculations respect the same distinction through these tensor contractions.

**Circularly Polarized Gravitational Waves**

This is a natural and beautiful next step from the plus (+) and cross (×) modes. Since you have experience working with polarized light in microscopy (measuring the difference between vertical and horizontal components and visualizing it), the analogy to gravitational waves is actually quite close.

### 1. Quick reminder from light polarization (your background)

In optics:

- **Linear polarization** = light oscillating in one fixed direction (horizontal or vertical). 

- **Circular polarization** = the electric field vector rotates as the wave travels. It is created by combining **horizontal + vertical** light with a **90° phase shift** between them. 

- When you look at circularly polarized light through certain optics or detectors, the image or signal can show rotation or handedness (left vs. right). 

Gravitational waves work the same way, but instead of the electric field rotating, **spacetime itself** is being twisted in a rotating pattern.

### 2. How to make circular polarization from + and ×

We already know:

- The **plus (+)** mode stretches horizontally and squeezes vertically. 

- The **cross (×)** mode stretches along the diagonals. 

If you add the two modes together with a **90° phase difference**, you get **circular polarization**.

Mathematically it looks like this:

εcircular=ε+±i ε×\\varepsilon\_\{\\text\{circular\}\} = \\varepsilon\_\{+\} \\pm i \\, \\varepsilon\_\{\\times\}εcircular​=ε+​±iε×​

(The “i” represents the 90° phase shift, just like in optics.)

There are two versions:

- **Right-circular** (or positive helicity) 

- **Left-circular** (or negative helicity) 

### 3. What test masses actually do

Instead of just stretching back and forth, test masses move in **circles**.

Imagine a ring of test masses in the plane perpendicular to the wave’s travel direction:

**Right-circular gravitational wave (one full cycle):**

text

Copy

```
`Phase 0°     Phase 45°     Phase 90°     Phase 135°`

`   ●           ●             ●             ●`

` ●   ●       ●     ●       ●       ●     ●     ●`

`●     ●     ●       ●     ●         ●   ●       ●`

` ●   ●       ●     ●       ●       ●     ●     ●`

`   ●           ●             ●             ●`


`(The pattern rotates clockwise or counterclockwise depending on convention)`
```

Each test mass traces out a small **circle** as the wave passes. The whole ring appears to rotate while also breathing in and out slightly.

This is directly analogous to how the electric field vector in circularly polarized light rotates.

### 4. Handedness (Left vs Right)

Just like with light, gravitational waves have two possible **handednesses**:

| **Handedness** | **Phase relationship** | **Rotation direction of test masses** | Graviton helicity |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| **Right-circular** | + and × with +90° shift | One direction | +2 |
| **Left-circular** | + and × with -90° shift | Opposite direction | -2 |

In general relativity, a massless graviton can only have helicity **+2** or **-2** (it cannot have helicity 0 or ±1). This is why we only get these two circular modes.

### 5. Why this matters

- **In observations**: Most astrophysical sources (binary black hole mergers) produce a mixture of linear and circular polarization depending on the orientation of the system relative to Earth. Future detectors may be able to measure the circular component, which carries information about the spin of the merging objects. 

- **In theory**: Circular polarization corresponds directly to the **helicity** (spin projection along the direction of motion) of the graviton. This is important in scattering amplitude calculations and in the double-copy story, because the kinematic factors must correctly reproduce these helicity states. 

- **In your microscope experience**: Just as you could separate vertical and horizontal polarization and visualize their difference, in principle one could design a “gravitational wave polarimeter” that separates the + and × components (or the left- and right-circular components). LIGO already does something similar by combining signals from multiple detectors. 

### 6. Simple way to remember it

- **Linear polarization** (+ or ×) = back-and-forth stretching (like your vertical vs horizontal light). 

- **Circular polarization** = the stretching direction **rotates** as the wave passes (like circularly polarized light where the electric field spins). 

The two linear modes (+ and ×) are the “basis states,” and circular polarization is just the complex combination of them with a phase shift — exactly parallel to what you already know from optics.

**v3.5.4**

**1. Punchy Title & One-Sentence Hook**  
Hawking Radiation Born from Gauge-Theory Pair Creation — Double Copy Induces Thermality and Horizon Dependence.  
They show that the full thermal Hawking spectrum in Vaidya spacetime, including its dependence on the horizon, arises as the double copy of ordinary particle production in a much simpler gauge-theory background that has neither a horizon nor a thermal spectrum on its own.

**2. Big-Picture Context**  
The double copy has long connected scattering amplitudes and certain classical solutions between gauge theory and gravity. Most work has stayed in flat space or static backgrounds. Extending it to dynamical black-hole formation and the quantum process of Hawking radiation is a natural but non-trivial step.

This paper takes a different route from the closely related electromagnetic single-copy calculation we analyzed earlier. Instead of working with an Abelian (electromagnetic) background, it starts from a non-Abelian gauge-theory setup and uses worldline methods to compute particle creation. It then applies the double-copy map not just to the background but also to the classical geodesics and the quantum mode functions.

The striking result is that thermality is not present in the gauge-theory calculation but is generated by the double-copy dictionary itself. The energy dependence introduced by the map turns a non-thermal spectrum into the familiar Planckian Hawking distribution. This gives a new way to see why Hawking radiation is thermal and ties the temperature directly to the classical double-copy rules.

**3. Necessary Background Crash-Course**  
**Worldline formalism for particle creation.** Instead of Feynman diagrams in field theory, one can describe a particle’s propagation using a path integral along its worldline. In a background field this gives a semiclassical wavefunction whose phase is the classical action. This is especially useful for high-energy or semiclassical limits. Analogy: think of it as following the “most probable path” a signal takes through a time-varying transmission line, then quantizing the small fluctuations around that path.

**Vaidya spacetime (recap).** A simple exact solution describing a black hole forming from a collapsing null shell of matter. Before the shell arrives spacetime is flat; after it passes, a horizon exists. We already discussed this in detail.

**Classical double copy on geodesics.** The map doesn’t just turn the background field into a metric. It also maps conserved quantities and changes in energy along trajectories. In the gauge-theory side a charged particle gains or loses energy when it crosses the collapsing shell. The double-copy rule converts that energy shift into the corresponding redshift experienced by a particle near the forming horizon in gravity.

**Bogoliubov coefficients from overlaps.** Particle creation is quantified by how much an “in” mode (defined in the far past) overlaps with “out” modes (defined in the far future). These overlaps give the coefficients α and β that determine the spectrum. The double copy acts on these coefficients after the classical map has been applied.

**4. Core Technical Explanation**  
They begin with a gauge-theory background that is the direct analogue of the Vaidya null shell but in flat space: a collapsing shell of color charge that produces a Coulomb-like potential after it passes. There is no event horizon — only a singularity at the origin.

They first solve the classical problem of massless probe particles (geodesics) in this background. When a particle crosses the shell it experiences an energy shift. The double-copy rules map this shift to the energy change a particle would feel in the gravitational Vaidya spacetime, including the redshift factor that depends on how close it passes to the would-be horizon.

They then lift this to the quantum level using the worldline formalism. The semiclassical wavefunction of an outgoing particle acquires a phase that includes both the usual propagation term and the integrated effect of the background. Applying the double-copy map to this phase produces the corresponding wavefunction in Vaidya.

To extract the spectrum they compute the Bogoliubov coefficients from the overlap between incoming and outgoing modes. On the gauge-theory side the mid-time (high-redshift) spectrum is non-thermal. They also perform an exact calculation in the gauge theory using Whittaker functions and confirm that the semiclassical limit recovers the thermal result after double copy. The singularity at the origin in the gauge theory plays a role analogous to the horizon in gravity under the map.

**5. What’s Genuinely New or Clever**  
The clever move is applying the double-copy map not only to the background but also to the classical energy shifts along geodesics and then to the quantum mode functions themselves. This induces the energy dependence that turns a non-thermal gauge-theory spectrum into a thermal gravitational one.

It unifies the classical double copy (on solutions and geodesics) with the quantum double copy (on amplitudes and worldline phases) in a dynamical black-hole setting. The paper also shows that horizon dependence emerges even though the gauge-theory side has no horizon — the map itself supplies it.

**6. Limitations & Open Questions (brutally honest)**  
The calculation is done in the semiclassical/high-redshift limit for the mid-time radiation; full back-reaction and late-time effects are left for future work. The gauge-theory background still has a singularity at the origin, so it is not completely “horizon-free” in every sense.

The exact quantum calculation is performed only on the gauge side; the double copy is applied after the fact. It would be interesting to see a more intrinsic double-copy prescription at the level of the quantum modes. Extensions to rotating (Kerr) or charged black holes, and to the information aspects of Hawking radiation, are mentioned as open directions.

**7. Three Crystallized Takeaways**

1. Thermality in Hawking radiation can be “induced” by the double-copy map itself — it does not have to be present in the underlying gauge-theory calculation. 

2. The classical double-copy rules on geodesics and energy shifts are sufficient to generate the correct redshift factor that produces the Planck spectrum when lifted to quantum modes. 

3. Horizon-like behavior and thermal radiation can emerge from a simpler gauge-theory setup that has neither, once the double-copy dictionary is applied consistently to both background and probes. 

**8. Detailed Summary & Explanation**  
The authors construct a gauge-theory background consisting of a collapsing null shell of charge in flat space. They compute particle production in this background using both semiclassical worldline methods and an exact solution of the wave equation.

They then apply the double-copy map in two stages: first to the classical trajectories and energy changes, then to the resulting quantum wavefunctions and their overlaps. The map introduces an energy dependence that is absent on the gauge side. When this dependence is inserted into the Bogoliubov coefficients, the spectrum becomes thermal with the correct Hawking temperature set by the mass of the formed black hole.

The calculation demonstrates that the double copy can carry horizon dependence and thermality from the gravitational side back into a simpler gauge-theory description, and vice versa. This provides a new window into why Hawking radiation is thermal and how the double copy extends beyond flat-space scattering into fully dynamical, quantum-gravitational regimes.

**9. Shorter Summary**  
By applying the double copy consistently to both the background and the probe particles’ classical and quantum dynamics, the authors show that the thermal Hawking spectrum in Vaidya spacetime arises directly from particle production in a simpler gauge-theory collapsing-shell background. The map itself supplies the energy dependence and horizon-like redshift that turn a non-thermal gauge result into the familiar Planckian Hawking radiation.

**The classical probe particles (geodesics) in the gauge-theory background and the double-copy mapping**

This part of the paper is doing something quite clever: it shows how a very simple *classical* calculation in a flat-space gauge theory (no gravity, no horizon) can be “translated” via the double copy into the corresponding classical physics in a real gravitational collapsing spacetime — and that translation automatically builds in the gravitational redshift that depends on how close a trajectory comes to where the horizon will form.

### 1. The setup on the gauge-theory side (“√Vaidya”)

They work in flat Minkowski spacetime written in advanced null coordinates (v, r, angles), where v is advanced time. There is a thin spherical shell of charge that collapses radially at the speed of light and reaches the origin at advanced time v = 0.

- For v \< 0 the space is completely empty (vacuum). 

- For v \> 0 a Coulomb field suddenly appears (like a point charge at the origin). 

A massless probe particle that carries charge q feels this background through the Lorentz force (or, equivalently, through a simple worldline action that includes an interaction term a · ż, where a\_μ is the effective potential felt by the probe).

Because the shell is infinitely thin, most of the particle’s motion is “free” (straight null lines in the coordinates they use), except exactly at the moment it crosses v = 0.

### 2. The classical problem they solve: what happens when the probe crosses the shell?

Before the shell arrives (v \< 0) the probe has some conserved energy parameter ℰ (essentially its frequency or energy measured by a distant observer).

After it crosses the shell the space has a Coulomb field, so the probe’s energy is again conserved, but with a *different* value.

The jump in energy, Δℰ, occurs instantaneously as the probe crosses v = 0. From the action or the equations of motion they find:

Δℰ = 2 g² q Q / v   (with appropriate sign conventions for attractive charge)

Here v is the advanced-time coordinate at which the particle is coming in from past null infinity (I⁻). The important point is that there **is** a sudden energy kick whose size depends on the charges and on how “early” the particle crosses (the v value).

This is a purely classical, flat-space effect — there is no horizon, no curvature, nothing relativistic in the geometric sense.

### 3. The double-copy translation to gravity (real Vaidya spacetime)

The double copy is a systematic rule that turns certain gauge-theory solutions into gravitational solutions. In this case the rules are roughly:

- Replace the gauge coupling factor g² with 2G (Newton’s constant). 

- Replace the product of charges q Q with something involving the probe’s own energy ℰ and the mass M of the collapsing shell: q Q → M ℰ (or more precisely M ℰ′ where ℰ′ is the *outgoing* energy after the jump). 

When you apply these replacements you get the corresponding energy jump in the *gravitational* Vaidya spacetime:

Δℰ\_gravity = 4 G M ℰ / v

Notice the crucial difference: on the gravity side the energy shift is **proportional to the probe’s own energy ℰ**. That is the seed of the redshift.

They also introduce a small shift in the time coordinate itself: v → v − v₀ with v₀ = −4 G M. This v₀ sets the characteristic scale of the horizon that will form (the horizon radius is 2 G M, and v₀ is directly related to that scale).

### 4. Why this captures “the redshift factor that depends on how close it passes to the would-be horizon”

In the real gravitational Vaidya spacetime a black hole forms after v = 0, with an event horizon at r = 2 G M.

Imagine two different probe particles (or, later, wave modes):

- One that crosses the shell far from the center (large impact parameter, never gets close to r = 2 G M). It barely feels the forming black hole; its energy barely changes. 

- One that crosses the shell on a trajectory that would have skimmed right next to where the horizon is forming (very small effective impact parameter relative to 2 G M). In gravity this particle (or the wave packet) suffers enormous **gravitational redshift** as it tries to climb out. Its energy at future infinity ℰ′ is *much smaller* than the energy it had near the shell (ℰ′ ≪ ℰ). The closer it was to the would-be horizon, the stronger this redshift. 

On the gauge-theory side there is no horizon and no redshift — the only thing that happens is the classical energy kick from the Coulomb field.

But because the double-copy rule replaces q Q with M ℰ (i.e. the shift becomes proportional to the probe energy itself) and introduces the time offset v₀ ~ G M, the *functional form* of the accumulated phase (the eikonal phase χ(v) ~ constant × log(−v)) on the gravity side ends up depending on the *outgoing* energy ℰ′ and on how close the trajectory was to the horizon scale set by v₀.

In other words, the mapping “imports” the horizon proximity information into the phase even though the original gauge-theory calculation never knew about a horizon.

### 5. Why they care (the bridge to Hawking radiation)

Later in the paper they promote this classical phase to a quantum wavefunction (via the worldline formalism or eikonal scattering). The fact that the phase now depends on ℰ′ in exactly the right way (with the exponential redshift factor coming from the log term and the v₀ shift) is what produces the thermal Bogoliubov coefficients characteristic of Hawking radiation when they compute the overlap between “in” and “out” modes.

So the seemingly innocent classical energy jump of a probe particle crossing a charge shell, once double-copied, automatically encodes the gravitational redshift that depends on proximity to the forming horizon — and that is ultimately what makes the radiation thermal.

**Simple analogy**  
Think of the gauge-theory Coulomb kick as a “sudden push” whose strength is fixed. The double copy turns that fixed push into a push whose strength is proportional to the particle’s own energy *and* whose timing is offset by an amount set by the horizon scale. In gravity that energy-dependent push + timing offset is precisely what a particle feels when it tries to escape from near a black hole horizon: the closer it was, the more its energy is “diluted” (redshifted) by the time it reaches a distant observer.

That is the deep reason the classical double copy works so cleanly here: it maps the simple flat-space kick into the curved-space redshift in one stroke.

**Lifting the classical picture to the quantum level**

After handling the classical geodesics and energy shifts of probe particles, the authors move to the **quantum** description using the **worldline formalism**.

### What is the worldline formalism here?

Instead of solving the full quantum field theory (Klein-Gordon equation) in a complicated background from scratch, the worldline approach treats the particle as if it travels along a path (its “worldline”) and computes the quantum amplitude via a path integral over all possible paths. In the **semiclassical limit** (high energy or short wavelength compared to the background scale), this simplifies dramatically: the dominant contribution comes from paths close to the classical trajectory, and the quantum wavefunction is essentially determined by the **classical action** accumulated along that trajectory.

This is the gravitational-wave / high-energy-physics version of the WKB or eikonal approximation you see in optics or quantum mechanics.

### The semiclassical wavefunction of an outgoing particle

For an **outgoing** particle (one that has crossed the shell and is now traveling away toward future null infinity), the semiclassical wavefunction takes the form

**2. Big-Picture Context**  
Black-hole formation and Hawking radiation are quintessentially gravitational, yet the double copy has shown for a decade that many gravity quantities are “squares” of gauge-theory ones. The authors ask: can we run the dictionary backward? Can we compute something that looks like Hawking radiation using only flat-space electromagnetism plus the single-copy map?

They answer yes. They take the simplest dynamical black-hole spacetime — Vaidya, a null shell of dust that collapses and forms a horizon — replace its mass parameter with charge, and obtain a time-dependent electromagnetic background that is literally the single copy. In that background they scatter a massless charged scalar exactly as one would scatter any probe field off an external current.

Because the background is Kerr-Schild, the interaction vertices are purely cubic and the ladder diagrams exponentiate cleanly in the geometric-optics limit. The resummed S-matrix element Fourier-transforms into Bogoliubov coefficients whose modulus squared is thermal. The same coefficients emerge from semiclassical null-ray tracing in the same background. The temperature parameter that appears is precisely the image, under double copy, of the surface gravity of the original Vaidya black hole.

In short, they have exhibited a concrete, calculable electromagnetic proxy whose thermodynamics, once double-copied, becomes Hawking radiation.

They do this replacement because the shared null direction k  k  k carries the entire dynamics; everything else is just a scalar profile ϕ  \\phi  ϕ. Analogy: imagine laying down a single fiber-optic cable (the null ray); gravity is what happens when you run two orthogonal polarizations down the same cable and let their intensities multiply.

**Vaidya spacetime.** A perfectly flat region for advanced time v\<0  v \< 0  v\<0, then an infinitesimally thin shell of null dust at v=0  v = 0  v=0 that instantly creates a Schwarzschild mass M  M  M for v\>0  v \> 0  v\>0. The shell falls straight to the origin; an event horizon forms immediately behind it. Analogy: a wall of traffic suddenly appears on an otherwise empty highway at a precise mile marker; beyond that marker every car is trapped in a jam that never clears — exactly an event horizon.

**Bogoliubov coefficients from a time-dependent background.** When the background changes with time, positive-frequency modes at past null infinity mix with negative-frequency modes at future null infinity. The mixing coefficients α  \\alpha  α and β  \\beta  β tell you how many real particles appear in the out-vacuum. Their ratio ∣β/α∣2  |\\beta/\\alpha|^2  ∣β/α∣2 is the number distribution. Analogy: slowly stretching a guitar string while it is in its quantum ground state; the stretching pumps energy in and real phonons pop out.

**Eikonal / geometric-optics limit.** High-frequency waves follow classical ray paths; the only quantum information left is the total phase accumulated along each ray. All soft exchanges can be resummed into that phase. Analogy: a laser beam traveling through a slowly varying fiber; you only need the optical path length, not the full wave equation at every point.

**Exponentiation of ladders.** Because the background is null and Kerr-Schild, every additional photon exchange with the shell adds a factor that commutes with the previous ones. The sum over any number of rungs collapses into an exponential, exactly as an infinite geometric series of identical reflections in a Fabry-Pérot cavity sums to a closed exponential transmission factor.

**4. Core Technical Explanation**  
They start with the single-copy background: an infalling shell of charge at advanced time v=0  v=0  v=0. The thermodynamic reading is then immediate: the number distribution is thermal with a temperature that is the double-copy image of the surface gravity of the original Vaidya black hole. The double copy has therefore supplied both the background and the temperature dictionary without ever leaving flat space.

**5. What’s Genuinely New or Clever**  
The single genuinely new move is to treat the classical double-copy map as a definition of a proxy spacetime and then do ordinary flat-space QFT on that proxy. Previous amplitude work derived Hawking radiation directly in curved Vaidya; here the authors show that the same thermal answer emerges from a gauge-theory calculation whose only curved-space input is the single-copy replacement rule. The exponentiation works “for free” because the Kerr-Schild structure is shared between the gravitational and electromagnetic sides. That shared algebra is what they call the “double-copy root of Hawking thermality.”

**6. Limitations & Open Questions (brutally honest)**  
The construction is tied to Kerr-Schild form and null collapse; it does not immediately extend to rotating or charged black holes with angular momentum. On the electromagnetic side the central charge is held fixed by an external force — there is no dynamical collapse or back-reaction, unlike real gravity. The entire calculation lives in the eikonal limit; strong-field or low-frequency corrections are invisible. The thermodynamic interpretation is suggestive but stops at the number distribution; a full entropy or microstate counting via double copy is not derived here.

Open questions that should be attacked in the next 12–24 months: (1) Can the same dictionary be applied to Kerr or Kerr-Newman single copies? (2) What happens when the probe scalar is replaced by a non-minimally coupled or spinning field? (3) Does the double-copy temperature survive once back-reaction or higher-curvature corrections are included? (4) Can the same ladder resummation be used to compute grey-body factors or late-time tails? (5) Is there a direct map from the electromagnetic soft theorems to the gravitational memory that accompanies Hawking radiation?

**7. Three Crystallized Takeaways**

1. The double copy is not merely an amplitude trick; it supplies a concrete electromagnetic stand-in for a dynamical black-hole spacetime whose particle-production spectrum, once double-copied, is exactly thermal. 

2. In the geometric-optics limit every ladder diagram with the collapsing shell exponentiates into a pure power-law phase whose Fourier transform is the Gamma function that encodes Bose-Einstein statistics — no curved-space calculation required. 

3. Hawking thermality has an algebraic origin visible already at the level of the single-copy background: the same parameter that sets the strength of the electromagnetic phase also sets the temperature that appears after double copy. 

**8. Detailed Summary & Explanation**  
The paper constructs the electromagnetic single copy of the Vaidya metric by the Kerr-Schild replacement 2GM→QB/4π  2GM\\to Q\_B/4\\pi  2GM→QB​/4π. It scatters a massless charged scalar off the resulting time-dependent Coulomb background, isolates the diagrams that exponentiate in the eikonal limit, obtains an all-orders S-matrix element, and extracts Bogoliubov coefficients that match those computed by ray-tracing null geodesics in the same background. The number distribution that follows is thermal; its temperature parameter is the double-copy image of the Vaidya surface gravity.

What this actually means: the authors have shown that the characteristic thermal factor of Hawking radiation is already encoded in the exponentiated phase that a charged probe picks up while flying past a collapsing charge shell in flat space. The double copy then acts as a precise dictionary that converts that electromagnetic phase into the gravitational surface gravity. Because the calculation never leaves flat space and uses only standard Feynman rules plus eikonal resummation, it supplies an independent, purely gauge-theoretic route to the same thermality that appears in curved-space quantum field theory. The match between the diagrammatic and ray-tracing routes confirms that the result is robust within the stated approximations. In the broader program of the authors, this is the next step after their earlier amplitude derivation of Hawking radiation: they have now exhibited the double-copy bridge that lets gauge-theory technology compute gravitational observables.

**9. Shorter Summary**  
By replacing the mass of a collapsing Vaidya shell with charge, the authors obtain a flat-space electromagnetic background whose probe scattering, after ladder resummation, produces exactly the thermal spectrum whose temperature double-copies to the Hawking temperature of the original black hole. Diagrammatic and semiclassical methods agree, demonstrating that the double copy supplies both the background and the thermality dictionary.

Thought for 13s

**The double copy is a deep, unexpected bridge between gauge theory (electromagnetism or Yang-Mills) and gravity.**

Here is what the sentence means, step by step, in plain language.

### Why black-hole formation and Hawking radiation look “purely gravitational”

- Black-hole formation (e.g. a collapsing shell of matter) is described by Einstein’s equations in general relativity. 

- Hawking radiation is a quantum effect that happens when you put quantum fields on that curved black-hole background. 

Both phenomena seem to require the full machinery of curved spacetime + quantum field theory on curved space. Nothing in ordinary flat-space electromagnetism or Yang-Mills theory appears to know anything about event horizons or thermal radiation from them. So for decades physicists treated them as quintessentially gravitational.

### What the double copy discovered (roughly 2010–2016 onward)

A hidden algebraic structure was uncovered, first in scattering amplitudes and later in classical solutions:

Gauge theory (Yang-Mills or electromagnetism) contains **color factors** (the way charges interact via the strong or electromagnetic force).  
Gravity amplitudes contain **kinematic factors** (momentum and polarization dependence).

There is a precise “duality” (color-kinematics duality, BCJ) that lets you replace every color factor in a gauge-theory diagram with the corresponding kinematic factor from another copy of the same diagram. When you do that replacement and square the result, you obtain the gravity amplitude.

In other words:

**Gravity amplitude ≈ (gauge-theory amplitude)²**  
(with color → kinematics)

This is not just a mathematical trick at the level of Feynman diagrams. It also works at the level of **classical solutions** of the field equations (the Kerr-Schild double copy that the paper uses).

### The classical version used in this paper (single copy ↔ double copy)

Certain gravity solutions can be written in **Kerr-Schild form**:

gμν=ημν+ϕ kμkνg\_\{\\mu\\nu\} = \\eta\_\{\\mu\\nu\} + \\phi\\, k\_\\mu k\_\\nugμν​=ημν​+ϕkμ​kν​

where ημν  \\eta\_\{\\mu\\nu\}  ημν​ is flat Minkowski space, kμ  k^\\mu  kμ is a null vector (k⋅k=0  k\\cdot k = 0  k⋅k=0), and ϕ  \\phi  ϕ is a scalar profile.

The **single copy** is obtained by stripping one factor of k  k  k:

Aμ=ϕ kμA\_\\mu = \\phi\\, k\_\\muAμ​=ϕkμ​

This Aμ  A\_\\mu  Aμ​ satisfies the Maxwell (or Yang-Mills) equations in flat space.  
The **double copy** puts the two factors back:

hμν=ϕ kμkνh\_\{\\mu\\nu\} = \\phi\\, k\_\\mu k\_\\nuhμν​=ϕkμ​kν​

and the resulting metric satisfies Einstein’s equations (at least for a large class of solutions, including the Vaidya collapsing shell in the paper).

So the gravitational field is literally built by “squaring” the gauge field in this algebraic sense. The same null direction k  k  k and the same profile ϕ  \\phi  ϕ are shared; gravity just multiplies the null vector by itself.

### Why this is surprising and powerful

- You can start with a simple electromagnetic configuration (a collapsing shell of charge in flat space) and, by the replacement rule above, obtain the corresponding gravitational configuration (a collapsing shell of mass that forms a black hole). 

- Quantities that are hard to compute in gravity (certain scattering processes, certain aspects of radiation, thermodynamic properties) often have simpler gauge-theory counterparts whose results can be “squared” to give the gravity answer. 

- In the paper you asked about, the authors exploit exactly this: they do the entire calculation of particle production in the electromagnetic single-copy background (ordinary flat-space QFT with an external time-dependent vector potential), then use the double-copy dictionary to read off the corresponding Hawking-radiation result in gravity. 

### Everyday-style analogy that fits the engineering mindset

Think of it like cache-coherency protocols in computer architecture.

A simple shared-bus protocol (gauge theory) has straightforward rules for how data moves between cores and memory.  
When you “square” those rules in a precise algebraic way (replace certain labels with momentum-like quantities and combine two copies), you recover the much more complicated cache-coherency traffic rules of a modern multi-core CPU with directory-based coherence (gravity).

The complex gravitational behavior is not invented from nothing; it emerges from the simpler gauge-theory rules via this squaring operation. The double copy is the discovery of that hidden mapping.

### Bottom line for the sentence

Black-hole formation and Hawking radiation are gravitational phenomena, yet the double copy has shown that many of their key quantities (background solutions, certain radiation spectra, thermodynamic features) are not independent inventions of gravity. They are the “squared” versions of quantities that already exist in ordinary gauge theory. The paper demonstrates one concrete realization of this bridge: compute the hard gravitational thing in the easier electromagnetic language, then double-copy the answer back to gravity.

That is why the sentence says “yet the double copy has shown for a decade…” — it has been a steadily growing toolkit that lets us import gauge-theory intuition and calculational power into gravity problems that used to look inaccessible.

**Color factors and kinematic factors — explained from the ground up**

You are right to pause here. These two pieces are the heart of the “hidden algebraic structure,” so let’s build them slowly with engineering-style pictures that match your background.

### 1. Feynman diagrams as recipes

When two particles scatter, quantum field theory gives the probability amplitude by summing **Feynman diagrams**.

Think of each diagram as a precise recipe:

- Lines = particles propagating 

- Vertices = places where particles interact 

- The whole diagram evaluates to a number (the contribution to the amplitude) 

In **gauge theories** (QED, QCD, Yang-Mills), every diagram naturally splits into two independent pieces that multiply:

**Diagram = (color factor) × (kinematic factor) / (propagator denominators)**

The denominators are just the usual energy-momentum bookkeeping you already know from QFT. The interesting split is between the two numerator pieces.

### 2. Color factor — the “which wire / which protocol tag” part

In electromagnetism (QED) the “color” is simply the electric charge Q  Q  Q of the particle. In the strong force (QCD) or non-Abelian Yang-Mills, particles carry **color charge** that lives in a more complicated group (SU(3) for QCD).

When three gluons meet at a vertex, the color factor tells you **how the color charges combine** — it is a number (or matrix) that depends only on the color labels of the three particles, not on their momenta or directions.

**Engineering analogy**  
Imagine a multi-core processor with a shared bus or network-on-chip. Every message packet carries a **core-ID tag** or **protocol label** (the “color”).  
The color factor is exactly that tag: it decides **which cores are allowed to talk to each other** and with what strength, completely independently of what actual data bits are inside the packet and how fast they are moving.

In short:  
**Color factor = the interaction topology / charge-group algebra part.**  
It knows nothing about spacetime, momenta, or polarizations.

### 3. Kinematic factor — the “actual data flow / timing / polarization” part

The kinematic factor contains everything that depends on:

- the momenta of the particles (p1,p2,… p\_1, p\_2, \\dots p1​,p2​,…) 

- their polarization vectors or tensors (how the particle is “oriented” or spinning) 

- the Lorentz structure of the vertices 

It encodes the **actual spacetime dynamics** — how the particles are moving, how their waves interfere, how angular momentum is conserved, etc.

**Engineering analogy**  
Continuing the multi-core picture:  
Once the core-ID tags (color) have decided that core A is allowed to send to core B, the **kinematic factor** is the actual payload — the voltage waveform on the wire, the timing of the clock edges, the routing delays, the polarization of the differential pair, the packet size, etc.

It is everything that lives in **physical spacetime** (or in the momentum space that describes wave propagation).

### 4. The hidden miracle: color-kinematics duality (BCJ)

In 2010 Bern, Carrasco and Johansson discovered that the **kinematic factors obey exactly the same algebraic identities** as the color factors.

Color factors satisfy the **Jacobi identity** (a kind of “triangle rule” for how three charges can combine).  
The kinematic numerators satisfy **the identical Jacobi identity** when you replace color labels with momentum and polarization expressions.

Because the two sets of objects obey the **same addition and replacement rules**, you can treat the kinematic factor as if it were a second “color” label.

### 5. How you actually “square” to get gravity

Take any gauge-theory (Yang-Mills) Feynman diagram.

It has the structure:

gauge diagram=C×ND\\text\{gauge diagram\} = \\frac\{ C \\times N \}\{ D \}gauge diagram=DC×N​

where

- C C C = color factor 

- N N N = kinematic numerator (momentum + polarization stuff) 

- D D D = propagator denominators 

Now do the following replacement, which is allowed because of the shared Jacobi algebra:

**Replace the color factor C  C  C with a second copy of the kinematic numerator N′  N'  N′** (from another identical copy of the diagram).

You obtain:

gravity diagram=N×N′D\\text\{gravity diagram\} = \\frac\{ N \\times N' \}\{ D \}gravity diagram=DN×N′​

That is the **double copy**. The resulting object is precisely a Feynman diagram for gravitons (spin-2 particles) in gravity.

In words:  
**Gravity amplitude = (gauge amplitude) squared**, where the squaring is done by swapping color labels for a second set of kinematic labels and multiplying.

This works at tree level exactly, and to high loop orders with some extra work. It is not just a trick for amplitudes — the same algebraic structure appears in classical field solutions (the Kerr-Schild double copy used in the paper you are analyzing).

### 6. Simple concrete picture (no heavy math)

Imagine you have a diagram with three gluons meeting.

- The color factor C C C tells you how the three color charges add up (like three colored wires joining at a junction box). 

- The kinematic factor N N N tells you how the three momentum vectors and polarization vectors combine at that vertex. 

Because N  N  N satisfies the same “three things combining” rule as C  C  C, you can take the entire diagram, throw away the color labels, and glue two copies of the kinematic structure together. What you get is the diagram for three gravitons interacting — exactly what Einstein gravity predicts for that process.

### 7. Why this matters for black holes and the paper

The same squaring structure that works for scattering amplitudes also works for **classical solutions** of the field equations.

- Coulomb field in electromagnetism (single copy) 

- → Schwarzschild black hole in gravity (double copy) by the replacement Aμ→hμν∝Aμkν A\_\\mu \\to h\_\{\\mu\\nu\} \\propto A\_\\mu k\_\\nu Aμ​→hμν​∝Aμ​kν​ or similar. 

- Collapsing charge shell in flat space (the electromagnetic background in the paper) 

- → Collapsing mass shell that forms a black hole (Vaidya metric) via the identical replacement rule. 

That is why the authors could compute particle production entirely in flat-space electromagnetism and then read off the Hawking-radiation answer in gravity by using the double-copy dictionary. The “squaring” operation maps both the background and the resulting thermal spectrum.

Color factors are the charge-group “wiring diagram” tags; kinematic factors are the actual momentum/polarization “waveform” traveling on those wires. Because the waveforms obey the same algebraic rules as the tags, you can replace every tag with a second waveform and obtain gravity — the double copy.

The same replacement rule that turns gluon diagrams into graviton diagrams turns the EM background into the gravitational background.

### Engineering-style analogy that makes the replacement intuitive

Think of a high-speed differential signaling link on a server motherboard.

- The **color factor** is like the VLAN tag or the lane-number label that routes the signal to the correct receiver. 

- The **kinematic numerator** is the actual differential voltage waveform traveling on the two wires (the real electrical signal with its timing, amplitude, and edge rates). 

Because the electrical waveform on the wires obeys strict rules (common-mode rejection, impedance matching, etc.) that happen to mirror the algebraic rules of the routing tags, you can do the following trick:

Take the routing tag and replace it with a second copy of the actual differential waveform.  
What you get is no longer a simple point-to-point link — you now have a higher-order, globally consistent interconnect whose behavior is governed by the quadratic combination of the two waveforms. That new system has properties (global phase coherence across the whole board, effective “curvature” in signal propagation) that are analogous to what gravity does with spacetime.

The double copy is doing exactly this replacement at the level of Feynman diagrams and at the level of classical field solutions.

### Why this lets the paper compute Hawking radiation

Because the replacement rule works for the background itself, the authors can:

1. Solve the much simpler electromagnetic problem (scattering a charged scalar off a collapsing charge shell in flat space). 

2. Use the double-copy dictionary to translate the result directly into the corresponding gravitational problem (particle production in Vaidya spacetime). 

3. The thermal spectrum they obtain is therefore guaranteed to be the image of Hawking radiation under the double-copy map. 

That is the mechanical reason the replacement produces gravity — both for amplitudes and for the classical backgrounds used in the paper.

**How Feynman diagrams work in QED and QCD**

Feynman diagrams are a bookkeeping tool that lets physicists calculate the probability amplitude for particles to scatter or interact. Each diagram is a picture of one possible “history” or “pathway” the particles can take. You draw all the possible pathways (to the order you care about), calculate a number for each diagram, add them up (with the right signs and phases), square the total, and you get the probability.

We will stay strictly inside gauge theories (QED and QCD) — no gravity yet.

### 1. QED — Quantum Electrodynamics (the simplest case)

QED describes electrons, positrons, and photons. The photon is the force carrier. Electrons carry electric charge.

**The basic building block is the vertex:**

An electron comes in, emits (or absorbs) a photon, and continues as an electron.  
The factor at this vertex is −ieγμ  -i e \\gamma^\\mu  −ieγμ, where:

- e e e is the elementary charge (the strength of the electromagnetic interaction) 

- γμ \\gamma^\\mu γμ are Dirac matrices that handle the spin of the electron 

- The −i -i −i is a conventional phase from the Feynman rules 

**Propagators** (the lines):

- Electron/positron line: i/(p̸−m) i / (\\not\{p\} - m) i/(p−m) (the Dirac propagator) 

- Photon line: −igμν/q2 -i g\_\{\\mu\\nu\} / q^2 −igμν​/q2 (in Feynman gauge) 

Here is a clean tree-level QED diagram for the process e+e−→μ+μ−  e^+ e^- \\to \\mu^+ \\mu^-  e+e−→μ+μ− (electron-positron annihilation into a muon-antimuon pair via a virtual photon):

[IMAGE REMOVED] – Feynman Diagrams")

Basic QED processes (LO) – Feynman Diagrams

**What this diagram means physically**  
An electron and positron collide and annihilate. They produce a virtual photon that carries the energy and momentum. That virtual photon then materializes into a muon-antimuon pair.

The diagram tells you to multiply:

- The two electron-photon vertices (each contributes −ieγμ -i e \\gamma^\\mu −ieγμ) 

- The muon-photon vertices (same factor) 

- The photon propagator in the middle (−igμν/q2 -i g\_\{\\mu\\nu\} / q^2 −igμν​/q2) 

- The external particle wave functions (spinors for the incoming/outgoing fermions) 

You evaluate this expression, square it, integrate over phase space, and you get the probability for this process to happen at this order in perturbation theory.

In QED the photon has **no charge of its own**, so there are no extra “color” labels on the photon line. The only factors that appear are the electric charges e  e  e at each vertex and the kinematic/spin factors from the Dirac matrices and momenta. There is no separate “color factor” that lives in its own algebra.

### 2. QCD — Quantum Chromodynamics (where color factors appear)

QCD describes quarks and gluons. Quarks come in three colors (red, green, blue — a label, not real color). Gluons are the force carriers and they **themselves carry color charge**. This is the key difference from QED.

There are eight types of gluons, labeled by an index a=1,…,8  a = 1, \\dots, 8  a=1,…,8.

**The quark-gluon vertex** looks similar to the QED vertex but now carries color:

A quark with color index i  i  i emits or absorbs a gluon with color index a  a  a and becomes a quark with color index j  j  j.  
The factor at the vertex is −igsTijaγμ  -i g\_s T^a\_\{ij\} \\gamma^\\mu  −igs​Tija​γμ, where:

- gs g\_s gs​ is the strong coupling constant 

- Tija T^a\_\{ij\} Tija​ are the generators of SU(3) (3×3 matrices, one for each gluon color a a a) 

- The indices i,j i, j i,j run over the three quark colors 

**Gluon self-interaction vertices** also exist (three-gluon and four-gluon vertices) because gluons carry color. These involve the structure constants fabc  f^\{abc\}  fabc of the SU(3) group.

**A simple QCD example: quark-quark scattering via gluon exchange**

Imagine two quarks scattering by exchanging a single gluon (tree level, t-channel).

The diagram has:

- Two quark lines coming in, exchanging a gluon, and going out 

- At each quark-gluon vertex there is a factor Ta T^a Ta 

- The gluon propagator carries color index a a a 

When you calculate the contribution of this diagram, it factors cleanly into two independent pieces:

QCD diagram=(color factor C)×(kinematic factor N)propagator denominators\\text\{QCD diagram\} = \\frac\{ (\\text\{color factor \} C) \\times (\\text\{kinematic factor \} N) \}\{ \\text\{propagator denominators\} \}QCD diagram=propagator denominators(color factor C)×(kinematic factor N)​

- **Color factor C C C**: Comes from contracting the color matrices at the two vertices, e.g. TijaTkla T^a\_\{ij\} T^a\_\{kl\} Tija​Tkla​ (sum over the gluon color a a a). It is a pure number (or matrix in color space) that depends only on which colors the quarks have. It knows nothing about momenta or spins. 

- **Kinematic factor N N N**: Contains all the Dirac matrices, gamma structures, momenta flowing through the gluon, and polarization sums if the gluon is external. This is exactly analogous to the QED calculation but now with the strong coupling gs g\_s gs​. 

The color factor C  C  C lives in its own algebra (the Lie algebra of SU(3)). The kinematic factor lives in spacetime. They multiply because the full Feynman rule is a product of the color part and the spacetime part.

This separation is automatic in QCD because the color is carried by the group indices on the gluons and quarks, while the momentum and spin live on the Lorentz indices.

In QED there is essentially only one kind of factor at the vertex (the charge e  e  e) and no non-trivial color algebra.

These color factors obey algebraic identities (Jacobi identity, antisymmetry). That algebra is what later allows the “swap” with kinematic factors in the double-copy story — but we are not there yet.

| QED | Photon | No | Just the number e e e | Momenta + Dirac matrices |
| QCD | Gluon | Yes (color charge) | Tija T^a\_\{ij\} Tija​ or fabc f^\{abc\} fabc | Momenta + Dirac + polarization |

Feynman diagrams in both theories are evaluated the same way: multiply the factors at every vertex and propagator, sum over all diagrams that contribute to the process, square the total amplitude, and integrate.
